note: Set A binds the key elevations and vertical relationships correctly (GRADE LEVEL 0", FIRST FLR 2'-4", T.O. STEEL 11'-4", the 2'-4" grade-to-floor and 9'-0" floor-to-steel spans) and keeps section-specific dimensions such as 1'-3" in Structural Section 2 and 7'-6" between grids. Set B also gets the elevations right and adds the 37'-6" overall span, but it repeatedly attaches dimensions that appear in the C1/C4 sections (1'-8 7/16" twice, 8", 10", 1'-8", W10X15) to 'Detail A1', and it duplicates several claims (W8X13, L3x3x1/4", 1'-8 7/16"). Set A's weaker points are mislabeled references (C1 treated as a grid, 'Column A1', 'Grid B to Section A4') and a 6" dimension attributed to Section 1, but these are fewer and less systematic than B's misbindings. Both sets contain vague entities (e.g. 'horizontal member', 'structural member'), which A slightly outweighs with better condition retention.
